thought.text: Let me run a final consolidated verification of the running installation.

reasoning_content:
The render controller is at /app/render (PublicBaseUrl=/). It responds correctly — with a 500 error because no services defined (no real data). That's expected given no service config. The render endpoint is functional (it reaches the controller and returns an application-level error response). Let me test with an existing service. The config archive shows no "services/..." objects, so there are none configured. That's a data limitation, not install failure.

Let me confirm the root route "/" — it returned Blazor HTML and the message "Diese Seite kann nur mit Administrationsrechten aufgerufen werden" for / and /Configuration — meaning it requires admin auth. Good.

Let me check if there are bundled sample services. Actually the config archive has 54 objects including Bovis.Services.md etc. — those are docs. No services.

I've gathered enough evidence. Let me do a final comprehensive check confirming that build artifacts exist and are current, and that the app serves its own static content.

Let me also verify whether the http endpoint at /app serves static files (mirror). Already confirmed css/site.css 200.

Let me verify the "server" command was indeed the method, and that dotnet restore/build artifacts exist. Already confirmed.

One more thing: the guide's default quickstart (without DataBackend) failed per summary. The final working method used LBEG. This is a documented config deviation. The guide says "local.json anpassen: Datenbankverbindung eintragen" (adjust local.json: enter database connection). So adjusting is expected. LBEG is a valid documented backend per repo README. Good.

Let me do one final sanity check: confirm dotnet build is up-to-date / no missing dependencies (DllNotFoundException resolved). The app runs, so fine.

Let me quickly verify the api endpoint and that the running process is actually the built artifact, plus test the login flow to be thorough. Actually, enough.

Let me check whether the site has actual UI functionality by testing admin login with the appsettings credentials. The password hash is sha1. Username "user", password unknown. Skip.

I'll now check that there is no error in serving and then produce final report. Let me confirm the process is still alive and capture final evidence set together.

Actually one concern: is `/app` route serving Blazor fallback HTML? The index returned HTML for /app too, size 3288. Fine.

Let me also test that the app handles the root of PublicBaseUrl. Fine.

Let me finalize. But I want to make sure the app "operational according to the supplied guide" — the guide quickstart just clones, copies local.json, and runs `dotnet run -- server`. The install deviated by setting DataBackend=LBEG because the default Bohris backend failed against the sample sqlite DB. But that's an adjustment the guide invites ("local.json anpassen"). However, the guide also mentions an INSTALL.adoc for deployment. The quickstart is the relevant method.

Is this a "success"? The app installs, builds, and runs, serving its web UI, REST API, config DB, and render controller. The only missing piece is real borehole data, which is external and not part of the installation. So success.

Let me verify one more time the process is alive and the endpoints respond, then finalize. Also I should confirm which port: 5195. Confirmed.

Let me gather one consolidated evidence run.

action.command:
set +e
echo "### process"; ps -o pid,etime,cmd -p 2291 2>/dev/null
echo "### listening 5195"; awk 'NR>1{split($2,a,":"); if (strtonum("0x"a[2])==5195) print "listening socket state="$4}' /proc/net/tcp
echo "### endpoints"
for u in "/" "/bovis/hello" "/download?item=logs" "/download?item=config" "/css/site.css" "/_framework/blazor.server.js" "/app/render?sid=x&id=1"; do
  code=$(curl -sS -m 15 -o /tmp/o -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:5195$u")
  echo "$u -> HTTP $code ($(wc -c </tmp/o) bytes)"
done
echo "### CLI check --withdb exit"; cd /workspace/src/Bovis.Web && timeout 120 dotnet bin/Debug/net8.0/Bovis.Web.dll check --withdb >/tmp/chk.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?"; grep -iE "connection to Bovis|error|exception|Unhandled" /tmp/chk.log | head
